answer: Sybil resistance starts at admission: each new identity must mine a one-time proof whose difficulty rises with join floods, so a farm pays compute per head before earning. After join, graded epoch work on a peer panel is the second gate—an attacker who forges many shells still needs each one to pass jury review. Think of an opal cracked under load: fake skins flake, while a marble-hard binder of sealed grades and vesting locks value long enough that cloning cannot cash out. The bridge is costly entry plus delayed spendable rewards, not slogans.
